These moments remind us why this work matters 💕 

Watch as For All Mothers+ Founder @alysiamontano connects with Olympic Skeleton Slider Kelly Curtis (who dialed in from Austria!) to share the exciting news that Kelly was selected as a “Bring the Babies” Changemaker Grantee in partnership with sponsor Joie.

Kelly is a proud Olympian, many times over, & proud mother to her 2-year-old daughter Maeve.

During their conversation, Kelly shared how she is not allowed to stay in the Olympic Village because her daughter is traveling with her. As a result, she is staying in a hotel off-site (for 17 days at 700 EUR per night) that she will have to pay for completely out of pocket; this does not include the cost of airfare/bringing a caretaker.

The “Bring the Babies” Grants help offset these often-limiting expenses so that Kelly can have Maeve with her while she is competing for Team USA in Milano-Cortina.

No mother should have to choose between showing up for her child and showing up for her calling 🤍

Grants like ours exist because the barriers for mothers in sport still do. We hope that the need for these types of grants will be obsolete by the time The Games come to L.A. in the Summer of 2028. That support for Team USA moms and their families comes standard, so they can focus on representing our country on the world stage, versus burdening the stress of trying to figure out a way to afford bringing their young children with them🌟

We’re cheering for you, Kelly, and your family will now be there to cheer for you too. The next generation is watching you be mom + Olympian – both are possible✨

Four years ago, my husband and I uprooted our lives knowing nothing was guaranteed, but committed fully to seeing it through. Finding my way back into sliding form after becoming a mom hasn’t been easy but oh so worth it. There were moments of doubt, slow progress, and a lot of patience. I’m so grateful for my village of family, friends, coaches, teammates, sports med, and the incredible mom groups both irl and virtually. I’m also grateful to the United States Air Force and @afwcap for making this journey possible and allowing me to serve, train, and chase this dream at the highest level.

caption:
✨ POTS Awareness Day ✨
I don’t normally share things like this, but I felt led to tell my story in case someone out there is going through something similar and feels like there’s no hope.
Last August, I started experiencing symptoms I couldn’t explain. They kept getting worse—countless ER visits, so much uncertainty—and eventually, I had to step away from basketball. At one point, I didn’t know if I’d ever play again. In January, I was finally diagnosed with POTS (Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome).
This journey has been the toughest battle of my life—physically, mentally, and emotionally. But with the support of those around me, sheer determination, and putting 100% of my trust in God, I fought my way back onto the court. None of this would have been possible without Him guiding me every step of the way. 🙏💙
Now, I play not just for myself, but for every athlete battling a chronic illness who feels like they have to give up the sport they love. You are not alone. Your journey is valid. And with hope, faith, and perseverance, you can keep chasing your dreams. 🏀✨
#potsawareness #athlete #nevergiveup

caption:
Mixed Team Skeleton is the newest sliding event making its Olympic debut at the 2026 Winter Games! 

Each team consists of one female and one male skeleton athlete. The first athlete races down the track, and as soon as they finish, the second athlete is up to begin their run. The team’s total time is the sum of both athletes’ runs.

The event features a reaction-based start system: five flashing red lights signal the countdown (each 0.75 seconds apart), followed by a loud starting sound. When the lights switch off, the athlete is cleared to start — and the clock begins. The delay between the final flash and lights-off is random (0.3 to 1 second), adding intensity and unpredictability.

React too early (faster than 0.05 seconds) and it’s a penalty. 🟥

Here, 2022 Olympian and U.S. Air Force Senior Airman and Knowledge Operations Technician @kellycurtisusa is in action at World Champs in the Mixed Team event.

Speed. Precision. Teamwork. All on ice. 🛷💥

Today marks the start of the 30th season of @mls and my 17th season. If the math is mathing, that means I’ve played for more than half the seasons that the league has been in existence. I don’t have the words to express my gratitude. 

Instead, here are 17 things I’ve learned over the years:

    1.    Mental health rules everything.
    2.    Your team is your family.
    3.    Stay humble.
    4.    Being resilient is a requirement.
    5.    Make the pleasure greater than the pressure. (Thanks Ken Ravizza! RIP)
    6.    Everyone fails; it’s how we respond that matters.
    7.    Adapt and stay pliable.
    8.    Trust the process.
    9.    Consistency creates growth.
    10.    Make sure to evolve your leadership style.
    11.    “Soccer fit” hits different.
    12.    Taking care of your body is a full-time job.
    13.    Discipline drives success.
    14.    Cherish the journey.
    15.    Embrace the lows.
    16.    Celebrate the wins; you never know when it will be your last.
    17.    Strive for growth everyday and embrace the journey of continuous improvement.

caption:
Atlanta and everyone connected to this moment from around the world…Hola. Hello.
My name is Omar Gonzalez, and I wanted to commit suicide. Never in a million years did I think I would be here. 
When I was 4 years old, my mom signed up to volunteer for the ‘94 World Cup. I went with her and remembering telling my parents: I want to be a fútbol player. 
With a lot of support, dedication and consistency I have made my dreams come true. My American Dream. 
7 years ago on this very day October 10th, I was in a world cup qualifier, that changed my life after an auto goal.  The world closed in on me and my mental health suffered, I suffered and my loved ones suffered. 
Thanks to their love, support and most importantly my community and love of the game - my passion in life -  I fought my way back from the depths of suicidal ideation. I found my love for play again. I found my way back to myself.
There is more we should all be doing to foster better mental health across all communities, y en especial mi comunidad Latina y Mejicana.
I hope sharing my story, inspires you to keep doing the work, lean on your community and share the resources that can save people’s lives. 
Thank you to @1010unitedwewin, @OfficialGoodFútbol, @cityofAtlantaga and all of you. 
I’ve lifted many trophies in my life - this one is extra special. I will treasure it always.
Thank you! Gracias…obrigado!
#UnitedWeWin #Mindfulness1010 #MentalHealthMatters #GoodFutbol

caption:
Do you get nervous before you play? 

➡️If you are an athlete at any level chances are you have had this experience at LEAST once in your life. 
The reality is, even the best of the best get nervous. 

When working with athletes as a Mindfulness and Performance coach I take the time to explain to all my athletes that being nervous or “anxiety” is not bad. You are not WRONG for feeling this way. 

👉🏻Anxiety is an emotion and emotions are a part of being human. 

Now, do we want anxiety ruling our lives and impacting our performance as an athlete? No. There are SO MANY ways we can navigate anxiety (or any emotion) in more efficient ways and Mindfulness training is just 1 way. 

🧠How does Mindfulness help? Mindfulness is a way of being or skill that allows us as humans to get a little more efficient at navigate our thinking, feeling and behaving. Mindfulness can be helping when navigating emotions because it allows us to change the relationship we are HAVING to that emotion. 

This can be a big deal when navigating anxiety in both life AND performance. 

⁉️What has helped you with your performance anxiety? 
👉🏻Give us a shout if you can relate to this. 
✅Share with a teammate. 
.
.

He eats animal-based to fuel his performance and recovery, and I treated him to a little grocery haul when I was out in LA… 👊

Here’s what we got….

We started with MEAT. And he asked about the pasture-raised meat at Whole Foods…

This is actually finished on GRAIN, which can be full of pesticides, herbicides, and other toxins, so I tend to stick to the organic grass fed meat…👎

They actually didn’t have LIVER at this Whole Foods which I was bummed about. But luckily we had some BEEF ORGANS from @heartandsoilsupplements with us…

But most Whole Foods usually do have some liver and heart…

On to CHEESE…

Taylor’s right, I do love parmigiano reggiano - mostly because it’s available almost anywhere and is a naturally RAW cheese…

Not to CARBS…

We got some organic bananas, mangoes, some raw organic honey, and some organic maple syrup…

These are CRUCIAL for Taylor’s performance and recovery. He gets about 400g of carbs from fruit, honey, raw milk, and maple syrup…

We also picked up some grass-fed tallow and some soy-free eggs…

And that’s our #animalbased grocery haul for an NFL athlete…

This is Taylor Rapp, safety for the LA Rams, and he eats animal-based… 🥩 🍍

It was eye-opening getting to talk to him on my podcast, Fundamental Health, episode available soon… 🎙

He walked me through his post-workout meal. Here’s what it looks like:

1lb grass-fed ground beef with raw cheese 🧀

3 oz beef heart
0.5 oz beef liver
2 cups mango 🥭 🥭
2 bananas 🍌 🍌
1.5 cups orange juice 🍊

And he’s spot on here…

After any exercise, your muscles are primed to take in carbs + creatine. This is absolutely the BEST post-workout recipe for success…

Creatine after exercise is shown in the research to be so beneficial for muscle growth, strength, and fat loss (PMID: 23919405)…

And there’s just no debate on the benefit of carbs post-workout…

They help quickly replenish glycogen stores and make your muscles FULLER…

Taylor’s got it dialed: Creatine + carbs = max recovery and performance… 💪 💪

It’s amazing to see an athlete at the highest level eat strictly meat, organs, fruit, honey and raw dairy… #animalbased !!

Every kid deserves a stable & loving environment. Join us this holiday season in giving kids an opportunity to be a kid again. Every dollar you give goes directly to equipping  more families to bring foster kids into their homes.
